approach.method_basis: The Parent is a population-based genetic algorithm that works directly on molecular graphs and learns only from the scores it has actually been given in the current run. It starts from the ten supplied scored molecules, keeps the best sixty-four it has seen as breeders, and draws breeding parents by score quantile. Each proposal is either a connected-fragment recombination of two parents, with an optional finishing edit, or a short random walk of successive atom, bond and ring edits on one parent: that ordinary walk asks for one, two or three edits with probabilities 0.82, 0.15 and 0.03, raising its own minimum only after a long run of construction failures, and it stops at the first failed edit. Only the final product of an attempt can enter the candidate pool, and only after canonical-identity, duplicate and a narrow sulfur-environment admission check measured against the actual scored parents; direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process over radius-two chirality-aware integer Morgan count fingerprints, fitted chronologically to every accepted score with a generalized dot-product Tanimoto kernel and adaptive mean/scale normalization, then draws correlated posterior samples over the fresh pool and allocates the ten announced evaluations by Thompson selection. New real scores immediately update both the fitted archive and the breeding population. Every one of those decisions is taken the same way at evaluation twenty as at evaluation two hundred and ninety: nothing in the algorithm reacts to whether the search is still improving.
approach.novelty: The one mechanism added is a stagnation-gated step length: the generator keeps a single counter of consecutive announced batches that failed to raise this session's best score, and while that counter stands at three or more the ordinary single-parent walk asks for one, two or three edits with probabilities 0.50, 0.35 and 0.15 instead of 0.82, 0.15 and 0.03. The inherited law returns on the first batch that improves the best score, the saturation floor and the separate failure-driven escalation keep their original behaviour, and everything else in the method is untouched. What is new is the conditioning, not the dose. The lineage already measured the same lever as a constant law applied to the whole run, which lost score, and as a surrogate-guided choice between two candidate continuations, which lost more; neither asked whether longer local walks pay specifically when the search has demonstrably stopped improving, which is the regime the Parent's own receipts show covers about one fifth of its announced batches and carries its weakest increments. It also separates this position from the three siblings sharing the identical trigger on the same Parent: they change how much uncertainty the allocator weights, how many fresh candidates it chooses from, and whether two-parent recombination runs at all, while this is the only one that changes how far through structure space a single proposal is allowed to travel. The claim is deliberately narrow: more requested edits must first show up as longer executed walks and larger structural steps away from the generating parent, and only then can they be judged on realized accepted increments inside those stalled episodes.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent keeps drawing the same short local walk law when its own accepted feedback already says the incumbent has stopped moving. Its complete panel on n-1744a1494180 is macro mean 0.59645311428869 with population SD 0.03397032998399878 (seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287, 0.583088384937917), and the gain profile inside a session decays: mean best-so-far gain per session is +0.2402 over evaluations 11-100, +0.1054 over 101-200 and +0.0424 over 201-300. A read-only recount of the Anchor's own fifteen published trajectories (300 records each, 435 announced batches) locates that decay as an explicit regime: the consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter reaches 3 in 13 of 15 sessions, 29 episodes, 91 of 435 announced batches, mean 3.20 modified-regime batches per exited episode and a maximum of 8, with 4 terminal-censored episodes and no exposure at all in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2; at K=2 exposure is 15 of 15 sessions, 51 episodes and 140 batches, at K=4 it is 12 of 15, 21 episodes and 62 batches. Those 29 episodes also convert worst: their 25 exit batches carry mean sequential incumbent increments of +0.0191 against +0.0312 for all other improving batches, 0.4766 of the Anchor's 5.819415 total sequential incumbent gain, 8.2 percent. Inside exactly those batches the ordinary single-parent route still requests one edit with probability 0.82 (optional share 0.18, requested mean 1.21) from a founder-concentrated population. The surrounding evidence says the lever is real but state-blind: removing ordinary continuation on this Anchor loses 0.03069975142490533 over 41,716 exposed floor-one attempts (n-c070e95b09ef), while the one fixed run-wide increase to a 0.36 optional share lost 0.038954730839330654 (n-9d88f032c4dc) despite 14,479 multi-call pool finals, 669 of 2,888 evaluated multi-call ordinary finals and 308 later accepted offspring from 73 affected parents. Other-Parent removals n-dbee08307e86 (-0.02686763734135833) and n-29d770e728a6 (-0.019179888857869958) and the posterior-guided two-arm continuation n-87c89dda7e3b (-0.04808254201485503) bound the route further, and n-9f11b684e560 (-0.044213598377693675) shows the failure mode to avoid: 2,770 nonterminal next fits and 1,571 later breeders with positive gain mass falling 17.251535 to 15.276942. The single limiting behaviour this ticket responds to is that the walk-length law is constant in session state: the Parent spends its most expensive structural effort uniformly instead of where its own receipts show the local neighbourhood has stopped paying.

literature_review.conclusion: A fresh search found related work on raising mutation strength or restarting self-adaptive rates after detected stagnation, but no primary source that identifies a schedule, threshold or length distribution for this ordinary floor-one molecular walk law, and no official code release to integrate. The recorded source nodes hold no reusable review, so this review records a new search with an internal-evidence basis and no adoptions; the registered K and vector remain derived from the Anchor's receipts, and no asset or dependency is introduced.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The intervention is designed entirely from campaign receipts: the Anchor's own fifteen published trajectories locate the stalled regime and its exposure at K=3 (29 episodes, 91 of 435 announced batches, 13 of 15 sessions, exit increments +0.0191 against +0.0312), the removal control n-c070e95b09ef establishes that ordinary continuation presence is positive on this Parent, and the constant-law counterexample n-9d88f032c4dc establishes that a run-wide increase of the same lever loses. No published source supplies the threshold, the probability vector or the announced-batch trigger, so nothing is adopted and the design is internal-evidence based.

hypothesis: Make the ordinary single-parent requested mutation-call law state-conditioned instead of constant. Keep one integer counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches, defined only on this session's own accepted scores: after the ten initial records, an announced batch of ten is improving when at least one of its accepted members raises the session best-so-far above the value held when that batch was announced, otherwise non-improving; the counter increments on a non-improving batch and resets to zero on any improving batch. While that counter is at or above the bound threshold K=3, and only at saturation floor one, the ordinary route draws its requested length from rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.50, 0.35, 0.15]) instead of the inherited rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]), using exactly one active draw in its inherited stream position; the inherited law is restored for the generation of the first announced batch after an improving batch. Nominal optional-call share inside the regime rises 0.18 to 0.50 and nominal requested mean 1.21 to 1.65; on the same uniform draw the changed-length intervals have total probability 0.44 and expected added requested calls 0.44 per exposed floor-one attempt. Whenever min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80) exceeds one, the ORIGINAL [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] base draw and the original max(base, floor) schedule apply unchanged, so the rejection-conditioned escalation identity is untouched. Per-call internal retries, break-on-failed-mutate, single final-only admission, the original scored generating-parent references and the sulfur gate, crossover and its finishing mutation, parent sampling, survivors, pool refill, the count-fingerprint GP and the correlated Thompson allocation with its exact draw count and order all stay exactly as inherited.

finding_summary.headline: Stall-gated longer walks ran exactly and the panel gained +0.0076, but all of it is sitagliptin and longer-walk products carried little of it
finding_summary.insights:
The gate itself is the most transferable lesson. Because the Anchor's exact policy runs until a session has gone three batches without a new best, sessions that never stall keep their Anchor endpoints exactly. That includes the deco_hop seed-0 result of 0.856, which all 28 earlier complete-panel children of this Anchor lost by 0.22 to 0.28. A state-gated change therefore cannot lose ground in sessions where the search keeps improving, whereas every one of those earlier children gave up about 0.016 of panel mean in that one cell alone. That is a reason to prefer gated designs for any further generator intervention on this Anchor.

The longer-walk channel itself is only weakly supported. Longer executed walks are certain. Larger structural steps show up only in fingerprint space, not in molecule size. The allocator screens most lengthened products out, and the molecular review finds that the ones it does score often dismantle what the first edit built: 21 of 133 lose an aromatic ring and only 16 of 133 beat their parent. The extra in-stall gain was carried mainly by crossover and single edits on trajectories that had already diverged, and it is concentrated in one objective. There the molecular review ties the gain to piling fluorine onto compact fused cores, with oxygen-halogen bonds rising from 82 to 288 molecules, rather than to bigger single-parent jumps. No lengthened product raised the sitagliptin best directly, though one +0.068 step came from a direct child of one. So the campaign can now say that spending extra walk length only during measured stalls does no harm and, under these exact conditions, came with a small panel gain. It cannot say the longer walks caused that gain rather than the changed history that follows the first lengthened walk.

By its registration, this one exposed panel ends the schedule recipe: no probability, threshold or length sweep follows from it. What stays open is attribution. Would a gain confined to one objective, and only +0.0023 without its best cell, survive independent replication of the same code? Do lengthened products contribute anything beyond restarting the trajectory? The allocator's threefold down-selection of lengthened products also suggests that walk length is not the binding constraint while the count-fingerprint posterior filters out long jumps. The pending same-trigger siblings that change allocator uncertainty weight and pool breadth test that more directly.
finding_summary.results:
The switch behaved exactly as registered. Thirteen of fifteen sessions stalled long enough to trigger it: 33 stall episodes covering 96 of 435 announced batches, close to the Anchor's 29 episodes and 91 batches. Inside those batches the single-parent walk asked for more than one edit in 49.8% of attempts instead of 17.5% on the same random draws. Its mean request rose from 1.21 to 1.64 edits, and because no edit ever failed, every extra request became an executed edit. Outside the stall the requests matched the old law exactly. The two sessions that never stalled (deco_hop seeds 0 and 2) reproduced the Anchor's 300 records exactly. Every other session first diverged from the Anchor at the first stalled batch, never earlier. The saturation floor never rose above one, so the separate failure-driven escalation was never exercised.

The longer walks did travel further, but only modestly at the level of what got scored. The posterior allocator picked lengthened-walk products at about a third the rate of single-edit products (3.4% versus 10.4% of pooled candidates), so only 133 of 3,952 lengthened products were evaluated. Those 133 moved well away from their parent: median fingerprint distance 35 versus 20, and the scaffold changed in 74% versus 52%. Yet their median heavy-atom change was still one atom. Spread across all 608 scored single-parent products made in stalled batches, the median fingerprint distance rose only from 20 to 22 (mean 24.7, against 22.0 in the Anchor's own stalled batches), and heavy-atom change stayed at a median of one.

Stall episodes paid off somewhat better than the Anchor's. They ended after 2.94 batches on average instead of 3.20, only 2 ran to the end of the budget instead of 4, and together they produced 0.600 of best-score gain against 0.477. Gain over the best parent was 2.13 versus 1.64. The gain per exit, however, was unchanged (+0.0194 versus +0.0191). Of the 0.600, the longer-walk products themselves supplied only 0.052; crossover supplied 0.348 and ordinary single edits 0.193.

On the score, the complete matched panel averaged 0.6041 against 0.5965, a gain of +0.0076 that clears the registered +0.002 bar. Eight cells rose, five fell, and the two unstalled cells were identical. Seed macros moved -0.0082, +0.0183 and +0.0128, and seed-to-seed spread narrowed (population SD 0.023 versus 0.034). The gain comes entirely from sitagliptin_mpo (+0.019, +0.082 and +0.057; task mean +0.053). The other twelve cells average -0.0036, with zaleplon_mpo down 0.010 on average, and dropping the single best cell leaves only +0.0023.

molecular.headline: Compact aromatic amide, amine and fluorinated dione series whose leaders carry N-halogen, O-F, cyanate, nitroso and aminal attachments
molecular.overall_character: Node n-e5dba2059cfe emits recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks decorated by single-atom edits: 2-carboxamide indoles and dihydroisoquinoline imines, fused pyrazolo/imidazo triazine diones and thiones joined to 4-substituted quinazolines, coumarin-fused azaaryl ethers, 2-aryl diazepane and piperidine amines linked to halophenols, quinoline-linked piperazine-2,5-diones, and polyfluorinated 2-imino pyrimidinone cores. Rings, aromaticity, carbonyls and amides are abundant rather than missing. Across the 4350 optimizer observations (870 per task, three Search seeds, 300 accepted records per session including ten initials) the heavy-atom median by task is 25, 32, 29, 30 and 27 with overall range 1-96; the perceived-ring median is 3-4 and the aromatic-ring median 2-4. Digest ring-closure string incidences are 0.9655-0.9851 and aromatic-atom string incidences 0.9460-0.9747; those are molecule-level SMILES-text readings, not atom fractions. Fresh RDKit 2023.09.6 perception agrees that ring and aromatic content is real: 0 of 4350 strings are unparseable and only 89 have three or fewer heavy atoms. QED medians are 0.279-0.690 and SA-score medians 3.19-4.62, so the bulk of the output sits near ordinary drug-like size but with elevated assembly difficulty. Coverage is complete and paired. All fifteen trajectories of this node under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging/seed-*/trajectories/ and all fifteen authoritative published Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories under /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-*/trajectories/ were read in full, 4500 records per side, no path missing; context.comparison reports child_complete=true, paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch, with child_mean 0.6041007162263946 against parent_mean 0.59645311428869 and paired_mean_delta 0.007647601937704677. Those endpoint figures are quoted from the immutable comparison; scoring, ranking and activation are decided elsewhere and this report takes no position on them. The two panels overlap heavily: 2164 of 4500 records are identical in position and two of fifteen sessions (deco_hop seeds 0 and 2) reproduce the Parent trajectory exactly, so for those objectives there is no chemical difference at all to describe. The chemistry that differs is concentrated after each session's first divergence (evaluation 41-231 depending on session). The node's own passive walk receipts in the staging logs let the steps be read chemically: of 2808 recorded single-parent walks, 133 actually drew a longer requested length, and those 133 products move further in feature space (median count-fingerprint L1 35 versus 20) and change the Bemis-Murcko scaffold more often (74 percent versus 52 percent) while their median absolute heavy-atom change stays 1. The extra reach does not buy better chemistry: 16 of 133 exceed their generating parent's score, 21 lose an aromatic ring against 1 that gains one, 25 contain a non-aromatic ring with at least two endocyclic double bonds, and only 5 appear in the pooled per-seed top tens. This is a description of molecules, not a judgement that any mechanism activated. The liabilities are the familiar ones and they remain concentrated in the high-scoring molecules: halogen bonded directly to nitrogen in 706 of 4350 molecules (486 of them an N-F bond), directly to oxygen in 423 (366 an O-F bond) and to sulfur in 122, C-nitroso in 240, cyanate esters in 158, peroxides in 122, aminals in 312, and aromatic atoms inside four-membered rings in 501. Formal charge is absent from all 4350 molecules and no molecule carries an assigned tetrahedral or double-bond stereodescriptor, although 2508 contain at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre and 1132 at least one unspecified potentially stereogenic double bond; digest charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 on every panel. Two absences are panel-wide and checkable: no trifluoromethyl group occurs in any of the 4350 molecules, and every one of the 77 sulfonyl-bearing and 56 carboxylic-acid-bearing accepted molecules appears at evaluation 62 or earlier (median evaluation 26), so both groups enter with the shared initial set and are never rebuilt. No synthetic route, conformer, energy, assay, protonation state or extra oracle call was evaluated; apparent plausibility is a reading of the graphs alone.

per_task.generated_character: 870 optimizer molecules, heavy-atom median 25 (range 1-37), perceived-ring median 3, aromatic-ring median 3, QED median 0.588, SA median 3.19. The panel is dominated by one chemotype: a trisubstituted indole or azaindole bearing a 2-carboxamide to phenyl or 3-pyridyl, with methyl, ethyl and methoxy decoration and frequently a methylthio group. Amide matches occur in 652 of 870 molecules, aryl halide in 572, sulfur in 332 and fluorine in 596; basic amine centres appear in only 13. A secondary family replaces the pyrrole NH with a dihydroisoquinoline C=N imine, and a third opens the indole to an enamine acrylamide (164 enamines, 132 terminal vinyl groups). Sizes stay modest: the largest molecule has 37 heavy atoms. Synthetic plausibility is mixed - the carboxamide indoles themselves are ordinary, but 344 of 870 molecules carry a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds in 344 of 870 molecules and in 20 of the 30 pooled per-seed leaders, including the panel best CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C; an N-chloro or N-bromo amide is a halogenating reagent, not a stable amide.
N-N hydrazide linkages in 64 molecules, exemplified by the seed-0 leader CSc1c2cc(cc1OCCl)CC(C(=O)NN(Cl)c1ccccc1)=NC2, which combines an N-chloro hydrazide with a chloromethyl ether.
Alpha-halo ethers in 43 molecules (OCCl, OCF) and O-halogen bonds in 15; chloromethyl ethers are alkylating agents.
65 molecules contain a non-aromatic ring with two or more endocyclic double bonds and 63 place aromatic atoms inside a four-membered ring, both signs of ring edits outrunning ring chemistry.
21 accepted observations are fragments of three heavy atoms or fewer (FBr, ClBr, C1CON1, C) whose scores are 0.0, so part of the oracle budget is spent at the floor.
missing_features: No basic amine centre on a ring: only 13 of 870 molecules carry one, and none of the thirty pooled per-seed leaders does, so the panel explores a purely neutral amide surface.
No sulfonyl or sulfonamide chemistry anywhere in the 870 molecules, and no carboxylic acid; the polar-group vocabulary is restricted to amide, ether, thioether and halogen.
No N-hydroxy amide route is retained: hydroxamic acid matches fall to 5 of 870 from 112 of 870 on the published code Parent panel, whose own leader family used that group instead of N-halogen.
No trifluoromethyl or difluoromethyl group; fluorine is delivered as single aryl C-F (325 molecules) or N-F (188) bonds.
No assigned stereochemistry on any molecule, although 111 contain an unassigned potential tetrahedral centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The shared initial 3,4,5-trimethoxyindole-2-(4-fluoroanilide) scores 0.3051048083696145 and every session's leading family is a decorated version of it; the panel best is 0.4828171386373609 and the digest median 0.315299. What the gradient rewards is peripheral substitution of that one core: methyl and ethyl in place of methoxy, a 3-pyridyl rather than phenyl amide, and halogenation of the two ring and amide nitrogens. The reward is insensitive to halogen identity - CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C and CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Br)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C tie exactly at 0.4828171386373609, and eight further F/Cl/Br permutations tie at 0.46092619585962435. 390 of 870 molecules share an exact score with another molecule of the same session, and 129 have a sibling differing only in halogen identity, so much of the budget buys no new chemistry. Reactive nitrogen is not required: the seed-2 leader C=CNc1cc2c(c(OC)c1C=C)C=C2C(=O)Nc1cccnc1 reaches 0.433013 with a plain secondary amide, and COc1cc2cc(c1SC)CN=C(C(=O)Nc1ccc(F)cc1)C2 reaches 0.391806 with none. Size and heteroatom loading alone do nothing: the 37-heavy-atom tris(methylthio) molecule scores 5.09513e-08, and single-bond fragments such as FBr and C score 0.0.

per_task.generated_character: 870 optimizer molecules, heavy-atom median 32 (range 1-96), ring median 4, aromatic-ring median 4, QED median 0.279, SA median 4.17 - the largest and least drug-like panel. Three leading families, one per seed, and two of the three sessions (seeds 0 and 2) are byte-identical to the published Parent trajectory for all 300 records, so no new chemistry exists there to describe. Seed 0 builds a fused pyrazolo-triazine-dione/thione bearing a 4-linked quinazoline with an aryl O-F substituent and an alpha-chloro fluoromethyl ether on the imide nitrogen. Seed 1 builds a coumarin-fused pyridinyl ether carrying aryl nitriles, a cyanate ester and a sulfenyl bromide. Seed 2 builds a biphenylene-type framework, a benzene fused to a four-membered ring, carrying two C-nitroso groups, an acetyl and an alkoxyethyl chain. Across the panel: C-nitroso in 240 molecules, cyanate ester in 158, sulfenyl halide in 106, aromatic atoms inside a four-membered ring in 186, peroxide in 80, nitrile in 199, ester in 184, amide in only 21 and basic amine in 32.
liabilities: Aryl hypofluorite O-F bonds in the top molecule of seed 0 and in 20 molecules of this panel, with 43 molecules carrying an oxygen-halogen bond of some kind; an aryl O-F is not an isolable substituent.

Cyanate esters (OC#N) in 158 molecules including the seed-1 leader N#COc1c(CCCCl)c(Oc2cc(-c3ncc(-c4ncc(C#N)cc4Br)cc3Br)ccn2)nc2oc(=O)cc(SBr)c12, which also carries a sulfenyl bromide; 106 molecules contain an S-halogen bond.

C-nitroso groups in 240 molecules, carried by every seed-2 leader such as COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2, whose aromatic ring is additionally fused to a four-membered ring; 186 molecules place aromatic atoms in a four-membered ring.
Peroxide O-O bonds in 80 molecules and 19 fragments of at most three heavy atoms that still collect the 0.5 floor score, including SBr and BrSSBr.
Very large concatenations up to 96 heavy atoms and 19 rings raise synthetic and property questions that no score here answers.
missing_features: No conventional linker chemistry in the high-scoring region: amide matches occur in only 21 of 870 molecules and sulfonamide in none, so aryl systems are joined through ethers, direct bonds, cyanate esters and sulfenyl halides instead.
No basic amine centre in any leading molecule (32 of 870 panel-wide), and no carboxylic acid.

No neutral bioisosteric alternative to the reactive attachments the leaders depend on: the aryl O-F, cyanate and S-Br motifs are present in the top molecules of two seeds and the panel contains no comparably scoring molecule in which they are replaced by ordinary alkoxy, nitrile or thioether chemistry.
No trifluoromethyl group anywhere, and only 9 difluoromethyl groups, despite 513 molecules carrying aryl C-F.
No assigned stereochemistry, although 421 of 870 molecules contain an unassigned potential tetrahedral centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: This objective has a hard floor at 0.5 that any trivial fragment reaches: C, Cl, C=C, SBr and BrSSBr all score exactly 0.5, matching the digest worst list and the digest score_span worst of 0.5, while the median is 0.596454 and the best 0.8561477222467935. transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4350 optimizer molecules of n-e5dba2059cfe, read from the fifteen request-trusted staging trajectories, RDKit 2023.09.6 finds no trifluoromethyl group at all and only 12 difluoromethyl groups, while 706 molecules carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen, 423 a halogen bonded to oxygen, 486 specifically an N-F bond, 366 an O-F bond and 1556 an aryl carbon-fluorine bond. The same absence holds on the 4350 molecules of the published code Parent n-1744a1494180, so this is a property of the shared generator rather than of this intervention. The pattern is visible in the highest-scoring molecules, not only in the tail: one panel best is N=c1n(F)ccn(-c2ccccc2OF)c(C2(CF)C=CCN2)cc(=O)n1F with two N-F bonds and an aryl O-F, and another is CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Cl)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C with a halogen on both the amide and the ring nitrogen; 20 of 30 pooled leaders on that panel carry a nitrogen-halogen bond. Where single-atom halogenation is chemically harmless the labels are indifferent to it, since F/Cl/Br permutations tie exactly.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot place a multi-atom functional group as a unit; fluorine and other halogens arrive as isolated single bonds, including onto nitrogen and oxygen, and never as a trifluoromethyl group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the proposal operators a small vocabulary of intact multi-atom groups (haloalkyl, nitrile, sulfonyl, carboxyl, carboxamide and similar) that attach to a chosen heavy atom as one unit, and restrict single-heteroatom halogen addition to positions where the resulting bond is a bond type the generator already observed in its own scored molecules. Judge the change by whether emitted molecules gain complete groups, not by any score, and keep the operator blind to which objective is being optimized.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every one of the 77 accepted molecules containing a sulfonyl group and every one of the 56 containing a carboxylic acid appears at evaluation 62 or earlier out of 300, with median evaluation 26, across all fifteen sessions; after evaluation 150 neither group occurs once in 4350 molecules. Those groups enter only through the shared initial molecules, for example O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 and COS(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at evaluations 12-20. The same one-way drift shows in a hydroxamic acid family that falls to 5 of 870 molecules on one panel from 112 of 870 on the published code Parent panel, and in amide incidence that ranges from 652 to 21 per 870 across panels and reaches 0 of 330 in one panel's post-divergence window.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group vocabulary only narrows: groups supplied in the starting molecules disappear early and are never reconstructed by the search.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain an explicit inventory of the functional groups present in molecules the current session has actually scored, and give the operators a move that re-inserts a complete group from that inventory at a compatible site. Sequential single-atom edits cannot rebuild a sulfonyl or a carboxyl, so a group the population loses is permanently unreachable; the inventory must be derived from observed molecules, never from knowledge of the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Among 2675 accepted single-parent walks recorded in this node's own passive step receipts, 363 products have fewer aromatic rings than their generating parent and only 36 have more; among the 133 products of a lengthened walk, 21 lose an aromatic ring and 1 gains one. 754 of the 4350 emitted molecules contain a non-aromatic ring with at least two endocyclic double bonds, ranging from 38 to 344 per 870 across panels, and 501 place aromatic atoms inside a four-membered ring. The failure is visible in single molecules: CCNC(C1=CC=C(F)C(Br)OC1)N(CC)Cc1cc(CC)ccc1C, whose benzene has become a non-aromatic polyene ring, scores 0.026038 where its generating parent scored 0.9813, and 25 of the 133 lengthened-walk products carry such a ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring edits remove aromaticity far more often than they create it, and no move restores an aromatic ring once it is broken.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make the ring operators aromaticity-aware: check whether an edit destroys an aromatic system before accepting the product, and add the inverse move that re-aromatizes a fully unsaturated ring. A ratchet in which repeated edits on one ring can only degrade it is a property of the operator set and is correctable without reference to any objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This node's receipts record 2808 accepted single-parent walks, of which 133 actually used a longer requested length. Those 133 move further in feature space, with median count-fingerprint L1 distance 35 against 20 and a Bemis-Murcko scaffold change in 74 percent against 52 percent, yet their median absolute heavy-atom change is still 1, only 16 of 133 exceed their generating parent's score, and only 5 appear in the 150 pooled per-seed leading molecules. The largest observed losses are chemical dismantling rather than exploration: products that de-aromatize a ring or convert a saturated amine ring into an aminal fall from generating-parent scores above 0.96 to 0.026038 and 0.2444. This is a description of the molecules and their receipts; whether any mechanism activated is decided elsewhere.
transferable_gaps.gap: Longer local walks enlarge the structural step without improving the chemistry, because successive edits are placed independently and can revisit and dismantle the fragment the first edit just made.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A multi-edit walk needs site coordination: choose successive edit sites that are distinct and chemically compatible, and protect the substructure that the current scored population supports, so a longer walk produces a coherent multi-atom change rather than several independent single-atom changes on the same ring. State and verify this at the level of the emitted molecules, with no access to objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No formal charge occurs on any atom of the 4350 emitted molecules and no molecule carries an assigned tetrahedral or double-bond stereodescriptor, matching digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five panels. At the same time 2508 of 4350 molecules contain at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre and 1132 at least one unspecified potentially stereogenic double bond. The ambiguity falls precisely on the leading molecules: 2-aryl saturated-diamine leaders such as CNCc1cccc(C2NCCCCN2CCc2cc(C)cc(Br)c2)c1O and quaternary fluoroalkyl pyrroline leaders such as N=c1n(F)ccn(-c2ccccc2OF)c(C2(CF)C=CCN2)cc(=O)n1F are emitted with their centres unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no ionizable or stereochemically specified species: every molecule is a neutral graph with unresolved configuration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treat configuration as part of the proposed identity: either assign it where the operator creates a genuine centre or record explicitly that the arrangement is achiral or configurationally unstable, and keep protonation and tautomer identity as a separate declared question from stereochemistry. Neutral notation is a representation choice and should not be mistaken for evidence about the species that would exist.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Basic amine incidence varies from 13 to 529 per 870 molecules across the five panels, so the capability exists but is not available everywhere. On the panel where it is common, 246 of 870 molecules contain an N-C-N aminal and 245 an enamine, and the highest-scoring molecules are exactly those motifs: CNCc1cccc(C2NCCCCN2CCc2cc(C)cc(Br)c2)c1O is a 2-aryl aminal and CCCN1CC=C1N(C)C1NC(C)Oc2c1ccc(Cc1cc(Cl)cc(CF)c1)c2Cl combines a strained 1-azetine enamine with an N,O-aminal. Elsewhere the amine arrives as an N-alkoxyamine, as in CCCc1cc(ON2CCOC(=C3CN(C)C(=O)C(OCC)C3=O)N2)c2ccccc2n1, and panel-wide 312 molecules contain an aminal, 223 a nitrogen-nitrogen single bond and 448 a nitrogen-oxygen single bond, categories that overlap.
transferable_gaps.gap: Where the generator does build a basic nitrogen, it places it in hydrolytically fragile motifs - aminals, enamines and N-alkoxyamines - rather than in stable saturated amine rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add construction moves that build amine-containing rings through stable connectivity - a carbon between two nitrogens, an enamine or an N-O linkage are each distinct chemical environments and should be distinguishable by the operator - and prefer the stable alternative when both reach the same local neighbourhood. The distinction is purely structural and transfers across objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 89 of the 4350 emitted molecules have three or fewer heavy atoms, between 10 and 23 per panel, and they sit at or near each objective's floor: C, FBr and C1CON1 at 0.0, SBr, BrSSBr and Cl at a floor of 0.5, and F, CF and FCl between 1e-26 and 2.4e-23. Two of them are among the last observations of their session, including FCl as the three-hundredth record of one session and C1CCC1 as the two-hundred-ninety-ninth of another at 0.029484118479927362. The opposite extreme also persists: concatenations of 86 and 96 heavy atoms score 0.0288585 and 0.562821, below much smaller leaders in the same sessions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Accepted observations are still spent on fragments too small to carry any chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Bound the product size relative to its scored generating parent inside the operator, so deletion sequences cannot walk a molecule down to a diatomic fragment, and treat unbounded joining the same way. This is a structural guard on the proposal step, independent of any objective, and it should be verified by the size distribution of emitted molecules rather than by a score change.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
